utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the delay because of the technical problems. We might sit a little bit longer, which will be one hour and 30 minutes for each sitting or even a little bit longer. Maybe we could have one break. Yes, we'll try to do that. Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll just -- whenever you think it's time to take a break, just let me know and I'll stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the delay. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My name is Douglas Stringer. I'll ask you some questions this morning on behalf of the Prosecution. First of all, I'd like to ask the Registrar or the usher to give the witness two exhibits, Exhibit P11.18 and also Exhibit 14.3, which is a photograph. Witness, I think that you saw one of these exhibits previously, the one that's marked 11.18. Take a moment to look those over and then we'll go to work with those. Yesterday, Witness, you made some markings on a map that was a street map of the centre part of the town of Mostar. I think the one you marked on was a black and white version. Does the Exhibit 11.18 that you're now looking at -- does that appear to be a street map of the central part of the town of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, look at the other exhibit, which is Exhibit -- a photograph, number 14.3. That's not a photograph from 1993 or the time of the conflict. It's more recent. Are you able to recognise the areas shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Would this photograph appear to show a good section of the Bulevar in the town of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It can be seen. You can virtually see the whole Bulevar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And are you able to see the building that we refer to as the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, if I could ask you to put that photograph aside just for a moment and direct your attention back to the street map. Yesterday, you spoke about some units which were deployed along the Bulevar confrontation line during the conflict in 1993. You mentioned the ATG Vinko Skrobo, you mentioned also Benko Penavic, I believe, and I believe you also mentioned the 9th Battalion. Are those three units that you know to have been deployed along the Bulevar front line in Mostar during the summer of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the summer of 1993, well, this is a rather wide concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll suggest then, let's confine our discussion for this purpose to the period of time after the 30th of June. Let's talk about the period of July, August, September, 1993. Are we able to talk about units deployed along the front line during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I can speak for the period until the 27th, as far as Mostar is concerned, because later on, I left it and I left it for a short period of vacations. And then for a period of time, to become the commander of the north zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. I believe yesterday you testified that you -- there was a reorganisation and that you became commander of the north zone or the north sector in early July of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I became a commander of the north sector at the beginning of July. What I did say was that three sectors were established somewhere at the beginning of July, and I gave the names of the commanders for two sectors. Nobody asked me for the name of the commander of the third sector. I became north sector commander on the 25th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let's come back to this map. You testified yesterday about the ATG Vinko Skrobo. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You testified, I believe, that this was a unit that was deployed along the Bulevar in Mostar, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Parts of the unit were deployed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, taking the map and taking a pen, can you make a marking, perhaps, that would show us or indicate to us the area of responsibility of those parts of the ATG Vinko Skrobo that were deployed along the front line Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If you could perhaps just place a circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could you please place a number 1 above that line so that we will know that relates to the ATG Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, you testified -- well, let me -- just to stay with the ATG Vinko Skrobo, what's the time frame that you're testifying about? What's the time frame that you know this to have been the area of responsibility of this particular unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are referring to the period starting with the establishment of the sector called "town" and as far as I know, it -- prior to that, mixed units were deployed there, belonging to the 9th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the establishment of the sector Grad or town occurred in early July of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And did that area of responsibility for the ATG Vinko Skrobo that you've just indicated remain unchanged for the remainder of the conflict between the ABiH and the HVO in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know which conflict you're referring to. I spoke about the first days of July, and after that, I am not familiar with any conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, was there an armed conflict between the HVO and the ABiH in Mostar during the months of July through December of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I spoke about the aggression waged by the ABiH, and that was in sector north, on the 19th of September, 1993. And on the 20th -- 20th, 21st, 22nd, it happened in the suburb and areas of Mostar again, 20th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, the commander of the ATG Vinko Skrobo deployed at that position in early July 1993, was Vinko Martinovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Also known as Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, on one side of the Vinko Skrobo area of responsibility, a different unit was deployed. Would that be the 4th Battalion unit that you testified about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not the 4th Battalion on neither side. On the right-hand side, there was ATG Benko Penavic and on the right-hand side, the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. The 4th -- rather than using right and left, let's talk about north and south. Which of these units was deployed to the area immediately north of the Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Parts of the 9th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And did that change at the time of the reorganisation in early July of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think anything changed, and I am speaking about July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, if I could ask you to please take the map again and the pen into your hands, would you make a marking to show us the area of responsibility of the ATG Benko Penavic? And can you place a number 2 above that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It appears to me, sir, that this second marking you've made is an area of responsibility immediately to the south of the area of responsibility of the Vinko Skrobo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could take the map again with the number 3, give us the area of responsibility of the unit deployed on the other side of the Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, what's the unit whose area of responsibility is the area marked with the number 3? What unit is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Parts of the 9th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were there any military police units deployed along that part of the front line as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police was deployed further on, as far as I can recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The commander of the ATG Benko Penavic was Mario Milicevic, aka, also known as Baja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Benko Penavic had a headquarters located in a building on the Rondo in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The ATG Vinko Skrobo headquarters was located above or west of the Rondo on Kalemova Street. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not know that, and I never went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, I want to now ask you a little more generally about the positions you held and the areas where you were based.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And Mr. President, I don't know that I can do this without needing for us to go into private session, at least for the first set of questions I got. So I think, out of caution, to protect his identity we should move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Pages10252-10259 – redacted – private session

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to go back up now to the sector north that is in item number 2 on the first page and ask you some questions about those commanders. First of all, just so we know, this is happening on the 2nd of July, 1993, just within a couple of days after the Armija attack on the northern barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This order is being issued about two days after the Armija attacked the HVO northern barracks, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say how many days later, unless the date speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, okay. Let's go to it item number 2. There is a reference there to people who are going to be in command or hold positions of responsibility in this sector, north sector, one of whom is a Colonel M. Andric. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's Miro Andric, is it not, sir, Miro Andric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know him but just.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Wasn't he an officer with the army of Croatia, that is the HV, at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Miro Andric is a volunteer born in Herzegovina, and as a volunteer, he came in the very early days to defend those lands.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: For the usher, we are looking at page 1 of the English version. Yes, item number 2. Right there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Miro Andric had come down from Croatia and was commanding units of the HVO as a volunteer. Is that your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you say. I do not know if he came from Croatia but I know that he was there and that the story was that he was a volunteer, but I said I didn't know because I really knew him only scantily, only slightly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you don't know if he had been an officer in the Croatian Army previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I know something, then I say I do know it, but in this case because I'm not certain, I cannot say whether that is so or whether that is not so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. What about the next one, Colonel Cavar? Wasn't he also a colonel in the army of Croatia at this time, July of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards Colonel Cavar, I know that he was born in Siroki Brijeg, and that in the very beginning of the aggression of the Yugoslav army and reservists, he went back to his native Siroki Brijeg and commanded the brigade in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 661.01, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Cavar subsequently become a commander of the Mario Hrkac Cikota Brigade later in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was that a different person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I can give the witness my copy of the B/C/S version, if it would speed things up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, you're being shown now a new document, 661.01.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you put the English version on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, doesn't this document indicate that Colonel Cavar was in fact a colonel in the Croatian Army, the HV, as of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not my level to comment. Therefore, I cannot comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Well, let's come back to this Exhibit 492, which is the reorganisation document that we were talking about. Directing you back again to item number 2, those names that we've been talking about, another name that appears here is the name of M. Naletilic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And isn't that a reference, sir, to Mladen Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prosecutor, I am not an magician. I am an officer. There are at least 15 Naletilics whose first name starts with an M.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So it's your testimony, sir, that you don't know who this M. Naletilic who is referred to here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. Maybe the author knows, the one who wrote this, but I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, sir, isn't this Mladen Naletilic who is present in this courtroom? Isn't that a fact, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, this question now has been asked and answered two times and I object to the argumentative nature of this question. It's argumentative, Your Honour. He's just testified two times. There's many Naletilics with the first name "M." He doesn't know it, and it's asked and answered, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, first of all, I would like to say that it's cross-examination. The Prosecutor has the right to do that. But this is indeed, Mr. Stringer, the witness has answered that question. It's very clear. The message is very clear. I don't think you could go anywhere along this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, directly underneath this paragraph we have just been talking about is a paragraph that's number 1 in brackets. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, we have just been talking about the names which appear in paragraph 2. Do you see that, the names, Andric, Cavar, Naletilic? Now just going down to the very next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, this paragraph here, which is number 1 in brackets, this identifies the units which will form the units within this sector north, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Which includes units of the 2nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then moving down, that appears to be a reference to the Mario Cikota Siroki Brijeg Brigade, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Grude brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Tuta ATG unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about such a unit. There was no unit under that name during the war, and the brigade -- Grude Brigade, never, there was never such a brigade in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then continuing, a part of the Vojna Policija, the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on it. I do not know what the military police means.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, isn't this deploying part of the military police within this area of responsibility of sector north? Isn't that what's happening here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: HVO brigades received from the military police administration a squad or a platoon of the military police and they guarded headquarters, brought in soldiers who had deserted the front line or those who had failed to respond to the call-up for the next shift. I believe it is this police that they have in mind, the one which needed to operate in this sector north, which was 70 kilometres long.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Miro Andric commanded the 2nd Brigade forces, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Colonel Cavar, as indicated in the document we have just looked at, commanded the Mario Hrkac Cikota Brigade we just looked at, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mladen Naletilic commanded the ATG Tuta, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: There has never been a unit called Tuta, nor do I know commander Mladen Naletilic in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, if I could direct your attention now to item number 3, which relates to the defence of the town of Mostar. Do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then moving down two paragraphs to the paragraph marked number 2 in brackets, the following units are subordinated to the command: the 2nd brigade in the zone of responsibility defined under number 1, 3rd Brigade in the zone of responsibility defined under number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't follow it. I don't know where that is. Oh, I see. Item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, fine. Yes, you may go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So this appears to be placing certain units of the 2nd and 3rd Brigades into this area of responsibility and under the command of those sector commanders, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said already that parts of the 3rd brigade, 4th Battalion and 9th Battalion - and this is the ninth time I'm repeating it - were performing their missions in the sector responsible for the defence of the city, odbrana grada.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Continuing down, the Mostar ATG, bracket, from the Tuta ATG, closed bracket, and home guard units are also placed within this zone of responsibility, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but I've never heard of ATG Mostar, ATG Tuta, and home guard units, because there was only a home guard regiment in Mostar and it was made up of people over 40 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Mostar ATG would be a reference to the ATG Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you say. I don't know who is meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, one last question on this point: Those units of the 3rd Brigade which were subordinated to this command, they always remained within the structure of the 3rd Brigade, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Brigade was responsible, was duty-bound to provide shifts from its 4th and 9th Battalions, to provide shifts for men on that front line, which was manned by the forces of a platoon or so, not more than that, that is about 20, 25 men, and whilst they were performing their tasks on the front line, the command over them would be in the hands of the commander of the city, of the town sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I understand, sir. My question is a bit different. At all times, they are still members of the HVO 3rd Brigade, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and they are members of the 3rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The fact that they become subordinated to a different command does not mean that they are no longer members of the HVO 3rd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think my answer to that question was quite clear, and whoever served military service knows that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. So that these units were at all times within the HVO 3rd Brigade, even during the times they were subordinated to a different command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were subordinated to a different command and different commander at the time and while they were performing a task, but they were a component of the 3rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, are you aware, sir, that the Republic of Croatia was providing arms to the HVO during the spring of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 301.2, please? Could we put the English version on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's a good point. We should be in private session before we put this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I know, but do we need to put this on the ELMO since everybody has a copy of this document already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I didn't know the Trial Chamber had them so we can do without the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But you have to be careful.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Do we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We just won't put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this document? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise this document and I can explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And I assure you, I will give you an opportunity to explain it. I just need to ask you a couple of preliminary questions first. It's dated the 16th of April, 1993, a letter signed by you and Bruno Stojic directed to Mr. Gojko Susak, who was at the time the Minister of Defence for the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed this document, this requisition document, because I was in a position in which I could not defend the defence line facing the JNA and the reservists, because I didn't have a single round left, ammunition 7.9 millimetre round, and this was the ammunition required for the machine-guns, the weapon with the biggest fire power, and since the operative zone, upon my request, could not comply, and as a commander, I was responsible to defend this defence line, therefore I drafted this request in a provocative manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you were asking that -- or indicating that you would collect the ammunition in Pula which is in the very northern Adriatic region of the Republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew that in Pula there was a person born in Herzegovina, Mr. Anto Budimir who was the commander there. I knew him, therefore I put his name down. I knew no other name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So again getting back to my original question, the Republic of Croatia did provide arms and ammunition to the HVO during the spring of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that, unfortunately I never got the ammunition requested here either.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown IAC 22?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, if I could, let me ask you, what was your position -- actually, I won't ask that question because we are in public session and I think it appears on the face of the document anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: IAC-22?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this while we are getting the document, sir. Isn't it true that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, we don't have this document at hand. If you want to put the English version on the ELMO, we have to go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, paragraph 1.2 relates to the sector Mostar defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It refers to the defence of the town Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And among the units that is part of the Mostar defence is the Mrmak ATG. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is that the unit that was under the command of Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that this is the unit in question but I do not know whether it was called this way at that time because these orders were drafted and drawn up by operative officers, and it may have happened that the commander did not read all the orders through and simply signed it without having read the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you testified about the events that you saw and heard of in Mostar on the 9th of May, and I want to ask you some questions about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry to interrupt you. If you're changing your subjects, maybe it's a good time for us to have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break for 15 minutes. We'll resume at quarter past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, I failed to ask you one question about the preceding document which was Exhibit 590. Do you have 590 in front of you? Okay. And directing your attention, this is the order of Mr. Lasic dated 3 September, 1993. Do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Directing your attention to paragraph 1.2, this is one last question on the subordination issue that we discussed. Do you have 1.2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1.2, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If you could put 1.2 on the ELMO, please, in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, while the usher is doing that, you testified earlier that different units would be subordinated to the sector command. For instance, the 1st battalion of the 3rd Brigade here is subordinated to sector Mostar defence. And I believe your testimony was that despite the subordination, the 1st battalion always remains a part of the 3rd Brigade, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say anything about the 1st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I used the wrong word. It says here the 1st battalion, the 1st Battalion of the 3rd Brigade. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Brigade never had a 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Forget about the 1st Battalion, forget about the 3rd Brigade. Let me ask you this. You testified earlier that certain units within the 3rd Brigade were subordinated to the sector or would be subordinated to one of the sectors as part of the reorganisation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that parts, parts of battalions, when performing tasks on the defence line, that they would be subordinated to the highest command level of the front line, as long as they were performing these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: But at all times, they remained a part of the 3rd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention back now to paragraph 1.2. And I asked you about this earlier, reference to the Mrmak ATG or the Benko Penavic ATG, what are the units that those come from when they are subordinated to sector Mostar defence for these purposes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Certain elements of the 3rd Brigade are subordinated to sector Mostar defence, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the time when I was the commander of the 3rd Brigade, Prosecutor, and that was until the 20th of July. And it was very precise. I said which parts were subordinated to the Mostar sector, and since this here is the month of September, then I do not know exactly which elements of the 3rd Brigade were subordinated to the sector, and if that was the case at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Earlier in your testimony, you said they were subordinated to a different command and different commander at the time and while they were performing a task, but they were a component of the 3rd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about the 3rd Brigade while I was its commander, just as you are now talking while you are on this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, maybe you don't know the answer to this question --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the answer, but you are asking 1/3 BR. The 3rd Brigade never had any 1st battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this question: The ATG Mrmak which also forms of a part of sector Mostar defence, what unit does ATG Mrmak come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Prosecutor, here in this order that I really don't need to comment on because I did not make it, but any soldier, every subject, is indicated separately unless it is a special unit, a separate subject. Then he is or it is indicated through a particular number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Does the ATG Mrmak come from a larger unit or do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know what you want me to answer but I said that from this order, it transpires quite clearly that the ATG Mrmak and Benko Penavic ATG or the home guard regiment are the basic units which are not linked, which are not associated with any other unit, according to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Setting aside the document, based on your own personal knowledge as the person who held the positions you held within the HVO during this time, let me just ask you based on your own knowledge, this ATG Mrmak, was it associated with a larger unit or military group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, we'll move on, then, to the 9th of May and also some questions about the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Exhibit 413. Perhaps I should ask one question in private session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, sir, were you aware that hundreds of Muslim residents of West Mostar were taken out of their flats to various assembly points such as Velez stadium and then ultimately transported out to the Heliodrom, where they were held in custody for approximately nine, ten days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard that there were some prisoners but I did not know where they were taken because on the 10th and 9th of May, I was in the place called Krusevo organising the funeral for the killed soldier, Dragan Cule.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you're not aware whether hundreds of Muslims were rounded up and taken to the Heliodrom on that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know how many were taken and whether they were taken, all I know is that my brigade was never tasked with doing any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, that not only Muslim men but also women and children, civilians, were arrested by units of the HVO and taken to the Heliodrom on the 9th of May? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can talk about is what I saw, what somebody said, I'd rather not comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If I could direct you to the following day, which is the 10th of May, there is a reference in this report to members of [redacted] 3rd Brigade taking part in an operation to bring in and detain disloyal Muslims. Do you want to find that in the report, sir? 10 May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you is whether, in fact, members of the HVO 3rd Brigade participated in arresting and bringing in disloyal Muslims from the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prosecutor, I already said several times that some men were at home and did not perform the tasks. That is number 1. Number 2, you say here, disloyal. I don't know. I did not order to bring in anyone, but here in one place, it says very nicely, "The security service, with the help of unit, searched and brought in armed Muslims who had escaped from Jasenica." And in Jasenica there were only armed Muslims, those who were members of the 9th Battalion, and if they had fled from the unit, they could be dangerous in the depth and why they -- that is they left their units and if they were in the woods with weapons, then they were no longer troops belonging to the 9th Battalion. I did not say they were doing it but if they were doing it, then they were doing it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How do you define "disloyal Muslims"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: A member of a unit who, without authorisation, leaves his unit and takes his weapons with him, be he a Croat, Muslim or whoever. Then he's disloyal to the unit that issued him with the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What about civilians, sir? Isn't it true that disloyal or Muslims civilians who were viewed as disloyal were also arrested and brought to the Heliodrom on the 9th and 10th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men in my brigade had nothing to do with the civilian population but only with soldiers in their own unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask the usher to show you Exhibit P88 -- I'm sorry, P388.3. It's a document from the 12th of May, 1993. Sir, I'll remind you we are in private -- I'm sorry, we are in public session, so don't say your name, and I'll ask you some questions in a way which will not require you to identify yourself. Sir, is this a document dated 12 May, 1993, signed on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not sign it. It was signed by the chief of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Perhaps we should go into private session briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is a document requesting the release of a person who had been arrested and indicating that the further serving of his detention sentence is unnecessary. Would you know, sir, the reason why this document was issued?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't, but I'd like to propose that the Honourable Judges see the document, what it looks like, on their screens. I assume that this is a man who is a member of this brigade, left -- was brought in by the military police, and that he was to spend so many days in the military prison, in punishment, and then the request was made to set him free and you can see at the bottom who made that request and it was requested by his commander, whom I know personally. He was a Muslim, Semir Mustafa, and we have the number of his own ID at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I believe that the Judges have the document, sir, in both English and in your language. I want to ask you briefly about your whereabouts and some of your testimony regarding the 9th of May. My recollection, sir, is that you woke up early that morning when you heard some explosions which you subsequently concluded had taken place in the vicinity of the Northern Camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say near the Northern Camp. I mentioned that the direction in which it is, in which the Northern Camp is, on the direction of the Northern Camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And that you arrived, then, at the operative zone headquarters, I believe, at approximately 6.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That you then left from the operative zone headquarters and went out of town to a place called Kobilovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you took up a position with binoculars and watched events taking place in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Mostar but in the southern part, in the southern part, in the zone of my brigade's zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah, that was my question. And in fact, sir, you saw that there did not appear to be combat operations taking place in your area of responsibility, the southern regions below Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You then returned to the operative zone headquarters at about 7.30 or 7.45 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And that the information that you had about the events taking place is information provided to you by someone else in the operative zone headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the operations officers in the operative zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were not in the field at all on that day; you don't have personal knowledge of the events that were taking place in Mostar beyond what the operations officers told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I went then to Krusevo and then I heard what had happened in the city, in the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You're aware, sir, that the ABiH had a headquarters in West Mostar at a place called the Vranica building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You're aware, sir, that the HVO took control of the Vranica building headquarters on the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know whether he took it over on the 10th of May. I heard that there was fighting but I never went to that facility on the 9th or the 10th or the 11th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, whether Juka Prazina participated in the attack on the Vranica building on 9 and 10 May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know where he participated because it was very difficult to walk around the town at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did parts of the Convicts Battalion participate in the attack on the Vranica building during 9 and 10 May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was not aware that on the 9th of May, in the morning, anyone participated. I do not know that. All that people told me by -- that I was told by the operations staff was that people who were sleeping in their flats came out and opened fire in order to try to stop the break-through, but who was there, who put the defence together, who did it all, I cannot say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What time, then -- how long did you remain in the operative zone headquarters getting this information on the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a very brief period of time, because then I left to the Bijeli Brijeg hospital because I had been told that my soldier had been killed. And first I left to the Bijeli Brijeg hospital to make sure whether this is true, and then I left from there to inform the priest in Krusevo, Ljuba Planinic is his name, to tell him what happened, and together with me, one of the officers of my brigade went back to Bijeli Brijeg, Marko Cule, who was the neighbour of the killed soldier, Dragan Cule. He went with me to help in the preparations to take over the body and to organise the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So, sir, that by approximately 8.00 in the morning or so on the 9th of May, you left the operative zone headquarters, you concerned yourself with the arrangements, the things that needed to be done in respect of the soldier who had been killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you were not involved or informed of events that unfolded during the remainder of the day, the 9th of May, in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could be informed of what was going on but I couldn't see the events myself. I received information from my brigade because I entered into contact with them. We had a Motorola link with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Between the 10th of May and approximately the 18th of May, 1993, did you see Muslim prisoners at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw no prisoners because the gate to the military prison is the western gate leading towards -- into the Heliodrom camp, and since there were prisoners, soldiers, and God knows who else, members of the 3rd Brigade entered through the south -- southern gate and continued towards the north to perform their assignments, i.e. they went towards the airport. In principle, however, whenever I would enter the Heliodrom, I would do it by a passenger car and I never saw anybody there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll ask the witness be shown Exhibit 488.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, while you're looking that over, I'll just ask you a couple of preliminary questions. Does this appear to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Perhaps we should again quickly move into private session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document -- perhaps I could first direct your attention to the last page. Does it appear to be a document written by Bozo Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I cannot see the date on this document. I can only see a reference number. Could you tell me what is the date of this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I can't, because the translation that I've got does not bear the date either. Perhaps with that limitation, we can talk about it anyway. I can try to get a better copy in during the break, when we have the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Stringer, my colleague, just stated that he does not have a date on this document. The witness apparently cannot find a date on this document. But the exhibit list for this witness handed to the Defence appears to have, under Exhibit 582, a document date. I want to know -- I would like to know if this is just a mistake from the Prosecutor's Office or how this date arrived on this exhibit list handed to us this morning, when Mr. Stringer says he doesn't have a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I can supply the answer outside the presence of the witness. It would probably be safer. But there is a better copy that has the date. I mean, that's the simple answer. And it's just a matter of getting a better copy into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: But let me move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can come back to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, set this aside. Hopefully we will have a chance to come back to it. Witness, you've already described for us what was your area of responsibility beginning in late August or early September of 1993. I'll ask you be shown Exhibit P630. My question, sir, is just directing your attention to the last part of the document. First of all, this appears to be the report of an operations officer dated 6 October -- I'm sorry, 9 October, 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he wasn't [Real-time transcript read in error "was"] my operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting he was. He's an operations officer who is reporting on the situation on various front lines throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who is the operations officer. I don't see his signature. I see that the heading says the main staff. All I can do, Your Honours, is tell you about the situation at this location from which this gentleman writes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My question, sir, is whether this appears to be a report of an HVO operations officer reporting on the situation on various front lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't -- it's not an objection so to speak, but I believe this witness answered on line 8, page 52, yes, but he was not my operations officer. The record seems to appear -- appears on the record that they have him answering yes, but he was my operations officer. And I believe the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: -- said, "he was not my officer."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You're right. Mr. Stringer, would you please clarify this issue for us, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Maybe the court reporters need a break. They work awfully hard, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we could still go for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, let me as you a clarification on this because we might have gotten a mistake in the record. The person writing this is named Tomislav Naletilic based on what appears in the document. I know you don't know him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: He was not your operations officer, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was nobody's operations officer. He was a clerk in the main staff, and it just so happened that he was the officer on duty at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And in that capacity, sir, at the end of the document, he's reporting on events in the operative zone, South-Eastern Herzegovina, and at the very end, it says, "The planned mopping up operation was carried out today in sector north, in the area of Golubic. The operation was carried out by the Tuta ATG, the operation was successful and there were no losses and a group from the Vitez Ranko Boban Brigade took up positions on Golubic." My question, sir, is first the Vitez Ranko Boban Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We should go into private session, Mr. President, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we will resume at quarter to 1.00. We will have a 15-minutes' break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I apologise for breaking the flow of the cross-examination. And I agree with Mr. Stringer that, of course, the most important thing generally is to finish the witness. However, the Prosecution finds itself in a situation where I think we must raise this before the end of the day because it could be -- it's unlikely that we could either finish today or, in any event, that we will finish this week fairly soon and then not be in session again until next Wednesday. As Your Honours may know, yesterday we filed -- I don't know if it's made its way to your desk or not but yesterday we filed a motion a submission titled Prosecutor's Motion on Defence Witness Issues, which raises several issues. The most pressing one at the moment is as we stand here at this moment, we really have no certainty whatsoever who the next defence witness will be and/or who the defence witness will be next Wednesday, which is not a helpful, obviously, position for us to be in. What has been reported to us throughout this week is that apparently - I'll just general words - the proposed next witness, the witness who has been indicated for sometime as the next witness, has been hospitalised. Now, forgive me for being sceptical but the witness is here in The Hague and he's hospitalised, I have some doubts whether he will in fact testify next week. If that's not the case, Your Honour, then as I said, as I stand before you at this moment, the Prosecution has no information as to who the next witnesses will be. And from our perspective, Your Honour, that is not an acceptable position. And the reason I raise this to you now is that so, with some time, that is by the end of this session, or at the latest if we go into tomorrow morning, the Defence will certainly tell us, I'm sure, who the next several witnesses will be. I must only briefly also comment Your Honour, and I'm not going to belabour it, we received with some concern, the order about the secret Defence witnesses. I raise this only for you now. If it needs to be raised further, we can address it but I don't want to delay the proceedings today. I can only assume that in making those ex parte submissions to you, defence counsel, particularly Mr. Krsnik, advised you that the Prosecution had already agreed not to disclose the names of these witnesses to AID. If he did, that's one thing. If he did not tell you that, then we would object in the strongest possible terms that at an ex parte consideration of these matters, if it was not disclosed to the Chamber, that the Prosecution already agreed some weeks ago not to disclose the names of these so-called secret witnesses to the AID. But we would like -- the most important thing is we would like to know the next witnesses, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik? Mr. Krsnik, since that order is confidential and is ex parte filing, I'm not expecting you to comment on those filings. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this afternoon and tomorrow morning, the gentleman from the Prosecutor's Office will get the list but could we go into private session just for a second, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Please. But we don't have much time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As you know, today, there will be six cases going on and we have to be out of the room punctually on time. Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, will you please bring in the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to say thank you for hearing me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Over the break, Mr. President we were able to get a better copy of the one document, Exhibit P582, and copies have been provided to the Registrar. I'd ask that they be redistributed, I should say a better copy of the B/C/S version. So if we could put the better copy of Exhibit P582 in front of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, this is a document that we briefly looked at together before the break. You weren't able to see the date of the document. Are you able to tell the document's date now from the copy that's just been provided to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can now, the 28th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And sir, this is a document over the signature of Bozo Pavlovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know who signed it because I'm not familiar with Bozo's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Bozo Pavlovic became the commander of the HVO 3rd Brigade in approximately September of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, if I could direct your attention to this document, I've got some questions for you. This is a document entitled, "Report on the problems of the 3rd HVO Brigade," is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, wait a minute. The transcript says that we are in the open session, but from the monitor, we are still in the private session. Yes. We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, if I could just direct your attention to the very first paragraph of this document, where it indicates that the 3rd Brigade holds positions between the Buna River and the HIT department store downtown, but then there is also an indication that some positions between the health centre and the HIT department store are held by various ATG groups. Sir, do you know would that be a reference to the ATG Mrmak, Vinko Skrobo and/or ATG Benko Penavic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I do not know why you ask me that, since you can see that this is the report addressed to the main staff of the HVO, which I would have never done. I wouldn't have gone over the operative zone of East Herzegovina, and besides, I told you that at this time I was doing the reconnaissance and taking over the sector north, and I refuse to comment on this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, let me direct your attention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And while those are being supplied to you, Witness, let me ask you, I believe in your direct testimony you testified about military Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. operations which occurred in the village of Rastani in August and/or September of 1993. Do you recall testifying about Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not speak about Rastani in August, nor do I know anything about it. What I do know is that in September, on the 19th of September, the sector under my command was attacked and after that, the city sector was attacked and Rastani was there and the sector south, or rather Rodoc, Zenica, were attacked on the 20th but how long did it last, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's my understanding, sir, that the ABiH attacked HVO units in the vicinity of Rastani, that they captured the village, held the village only for a day or two, and then the HVO attacked again and was able to take the village of Rastani back into the possession of the HVO on or about 23 September. Does that sound roughly accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I did not know what -- how exactly it was in Rastani. I know my sector was attacked on the 19th and I learned that on the 20th some sectors of the city defence with were attacked. That is what I know about that. And I know everything there is to know about my sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The village of Rastani itself, were parts of the Convicts Battalion engaged in combat in Rastani during, say, the 20th to the 23rd of September, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 20th and the 24th, the Convicts Battalion was in a place called Vrdi and Ljubljana [phoen], or rather Jedrinje, where my soldiers were killed, and we were out to recover the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just in terms of the distance from the village of Rastani, what's the different -- distance involved?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, of course, I am not objecting because today my colleague Meek is doing that, but if my learned friend would be so kind, could the witness please repeat the place names that he said where were parts of the Convicts Battalion? The Defence believe that is this is very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's a reasonable request. Mr. Stringer, are you going to ask this question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To repeat the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, we need to get into the transcript a correct spelling for the locations you've just mentioned. Can you tell us, sir, where were -- where was the Convicts Battalion personnel deployed during this period of 20 to 24 September? Perhaps you could spell the names of these locations.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the Convicts Battalion reported to me on the 20th some, and some on the 21st September, 1993. I tasked some of them to go and recapture the front line above the village of Vrdi, Medved [phoen], Golubic, Aropovo Brdo, that is the summits of Mount Cabula. I ordered others to head for Jedrinje and Zarusje [phoen], to -- so as to ascertain how many fatalities had the second Siroki Brijeg Battalion suffered at the situation down there, and whether it was safe enough to send over there the home guards to take hold of the line. I know that they set off towards Jedrinje and left some troops in the village of Djubrani as protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, are we talking about fighting for the region which included the hydroelectric power plant that was north of Mostar, Rastani village, the hydroelectric power plant? Is this the area that we are generally talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not the area that I mean. I'm talking about the area where the 2nd HBP Selakovac is and then to the west or rather north-west of this hydropower plant, upstream of the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown P611, please? Witness, I think you already have that in front of you, sir. Isn't it true, sir, that the Kaznjenicka Bojna as well as its commander Tuta, received a citation from Bruno Stojic for the valour and combat skill displayed during the operations in Rastani during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that Mladen Naletilic Tuta was the commander of the Convicts Battalion. I told you who was the commander of the Convicts Battalion at the time, and as for citations, I cannot comment on the citations by the Ministry of Defence nor pass any judgements on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, sir, perhaps you are in a position to pass a judgement. Are you saying, sir, that Bruno Stojic was mistaken as to who was truly the commander of the Convicts Battalion, that he didn't know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, that question absolutely calls for speculation. This witness has already answered the question. He does not know about this. He hasn't seen this. And that is a speculative question and it's improper. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I disagree, Mr. President. This is cross-examination and I believe I'm entitled to test the witness on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We believe so. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, Bruno Stojic was the head of the defence department of the HVO. Now, if he wrote this, sir, is it your testimony that he did not know who was the commander of the unit Kaznjenicka Bojna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not what I said. I said Bruno Stojic is a civilian person, Minister of Defence, and I do not wish to comment his writings, nor do I have the right to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You testified that in June of 1992, the Convicts Battalion played a role in the liberation of Mostar. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned at least one of the soldiers of the KB, the Kaznjenicka Bojna, Cikota, who led a unit in those operations. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was he subsequently killed, sir, in April of 1993, in operations in the Jablanica area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know where he was killed but yes, I do know that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: As a result of the role played by the Convicts Battalion in the liberation of Mostar in June of 1992, did the Convicts Battalion -- did its prestige and the level of respect coming from others, did all of that increase because of its role in the liberation of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Convicts Battalion was the pride of the people because it enabled part of the expelled people to return to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In June of 1992, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, was associated with the Convicts Battalion; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And as a result of the success enjoyed by the Convicts Battalion, the prestige, the respect afforded to Mladen Naletilic increased as well throughout -- among Croats in the Herzegovina region; isn't that also true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a personal matter, and I cannot really speak what increased between the Muslims and Croats in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Didn't a lot of Croats and other individuals want to come join the Convicts Battalion as a result of the prestige it enjoyed after the liberation of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know whether they wanted it, because every one of them could know that they were very likely to be killed and they couldn't, even if they wanted to, because this was a special purpose unit with young, specially trained men.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, remained associated with the Convicts Battalion throughout 1993, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You say he was associated with the Convicts Battalion during 1992. Was he its leader?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't a leader of the Convicts Battalion, but I heard that he was one of the founders of the Convicts Battalion, and its chief, its leader, its commander, was Mario Hrkac, Cikota.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: As a founder of the Convicts Battalion, sir, isn't it true that Mladen Naletilic enjoyed authority and power in respect of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who had what. I didn't feel anything in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you saying, sir, that you don't know the extent to which Naletilic and Andabak shared responsibility in the leadership of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. I know Naletilic as a civilian, and that is how I saw him and how I perceived him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see him throughout 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, I did not see him. I did not see him even in 1992, after those liberation operations, because I went to Mostar and I was 40 kilometres away, and I do not know where Mladen Naletilic was. Once I asked about him and I was told that he had a casino in Zagreb, and that is all that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you go to Siroki Brijeg after your responsibilities and your new position came into place in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: During -- in the six months during which I commanded the sector north, I only three times went to my family, to Uzarici, and I was even less than that with my family, that is in Uzarici, even on Christmas and other holidays.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So having not seen Mr. Naletilic during 1993, sir, you don't really know what, if any, role or responsibilities he had during that time in respect of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibits P353, 457, 649, 732? Those will be the last ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to try to move rapidly through these. Although I don't want you to get the impression I'm trying to cut you off or to not give you an opportunity to explain, but we are all hoping that we can finish your testimony today so that you can go home. We've got about 20 minutes left to do that. You mentioned in your direct testimony that, I believe, there were no ranks and that also, as far as you knew, Tuta had no rank, he was a civilian. Now, do you have Exhibit 353 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, this is a document dated 27 April, 1993, proposal for awarding of ranks. Sir, do you know if, in fact, members of the Kaznjenicka Bojna sought and received ranks from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, here I can see the proposal. At that time, I was a highly ranked HVO officer and I only had the insignia of my commanding position, and I can show this to you through a videotape which shows me at a funeral. I had no ranks and I can hardly believe that anyone else had them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of this document, sir, it indicates that this is coming from the commander of the independent unit for special tasks, Convicts Battalion, the name typed, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, and then a signature appears there. Now, sir, doesn't this document indicate that in fact Mladen Naletilic Tuta is the commander of the Convicts Battalion in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on this. I know who was the commander, and as a military person, I can say the following. It is quite clearly said here, "signature," and I do not see any indication that somebody else signed on behalf of somebody else, which would be the "ZA" letters, and that was the practice if somebody else signed on behalf of another person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, we don't have the document and I wonder if perhaps they could put the -- the usher could put the English version on the ELMO so we could see the signature because there have been so many documents signed by Ivan Andabak where it's typed "Mladen Naletilic," so we don't know what this signature says or shows.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I can inform counsel, if no one is concerned about my doing it in the presence of the witness, it's not, I don't think, in dispute as to the person -- the identity the person signing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, so there is no problem to put this document on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes we will have it put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Put -- for the English, put the B/C/S version, the second page, or the -- I should say just the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could the record reflect that that document is signed by Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, why the document does not state that Ivan Andabak is the commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know why because I'm not the author of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is P457 and we could put the signature page of the B/C/S version on the ELMO for counsel, after the witness has had a chance to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, this is another document - now this is June of 1993 - requesting promotions for certain members of the Convicts Battalion. Do you have that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recognise this signature, and as I said before, the HVO had no ranks. If anybody, I should have had a rank but that time nobody had them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, doesn't this indicate, sir, that Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, was the commander of the independent special unit Convicts Battalion on the 15th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you who the Convicts Battalion's commander was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 649. Sir, this is a document dated 16 October, 1993, from someone named Stanko Bozic. This is a report indicating that on 13 October, 1993, acting on orders issued by General Mladen Naletilic, aka Tuta, a prisoner was taken from the central military prison to Siroki Brijeg for an interview with the named general. Sir, it's true, isn't it, that Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, was not a civilian, that he was in fact commander of the Convicts Battalion and a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you can go with me to Herzegovina, to Mostar, to Siroki Brijeg. Eighty per cent of soldiers who will meet me will greet me with a "general" and they will use general for the commander of a battalion or a brigade. This was a sort of sign of respect to generals, and if somebody wanted to address somebody that they respect, they would usually address them as general. And this is the practice even today, when you are received at a home, they will welcome you, "How are you, general?" There is a consequence of a war, this is a sort of special appreciation of generals, and I think that this is how we should see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, is it your testimony based on all these documents we have been looking at that Mladen Naletilic was a civilian throughout 1993? Is that truly what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I, as an officer and a man, can know is that he was a civilian, at least for me, and I'm sure that he could not issue a military order and thus could not be a commander of a military unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
