utterances.text: Having not seen him during 1993, though, sir, you could quite well be mistaken on that, isn't it true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not mistaken because I should have seen him somewhere as a commander of a unit, and I did not see him, therefore I cannot be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The last exhibit is P732. Do you see that one, sir? Did Ante Roso become chief of the HVO main staff in November of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't confirm this, nor can I deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: He replaced Slobodan Praljak who had held that position before him, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot define the period in which he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document dated the 29th of December, 1993, appearing over the name Colonel General Ante Roso, Chief of the Main Staff, directed to General Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, personally. Now, this is going to be the last document, and I want to ask you again now, having seen what Ante Roso is writing, isn't it possible, sir, that you're mistaken and that in fact Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, did hold a rank and was the commander of the Convicts Battalion during 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he had no rank and he was not the commander of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Would Ante Roso have been in a better position, sir, than you, to know the status of Mr. Naletilic during this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can assure you that had he read such an order, he would never have signed it. This type of orders were drawn up by inferior officers and very often their superiors would sign them without even having read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: But you don't know if that's the case on this document, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My question, sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- made in a manner which would not befit the chief of a general staff, because in this document, units are mentioned that had never existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: One of those being the Tuta ATG, which is identified in paragraph 5.1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. It -- this sort of a unit never existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seric? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from the Judges? No? Well, it's very strange. Thank you very much, Witness, for coming here to give your evidence. We appreciate that very much. We all wish you a good trip back home. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours, for enabling me to come here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any documents to tender, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, we have a lot of documents. Could we tender them in writing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that is a possibility, but we have received, I believe, all the documents with the English translation, and I hope we could do that after the cross-examination of the witness, later on, but if you prefer to file your applications, we'll do that. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that that's the end of this sitting, and we'll have a break and we'll resume again next Wednesday. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 1.40 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday the 24th day of April, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
